title: introduce-kernel-stability-thresholds-and-precision-annealing-with-kv-sync-guard
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds kernel stability probes, a precision-annealing state machine, and a kv-sync guard to reduce correctness regressions when switching to low-precision fast paths; safe defaults and canary rollout enabled.
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent correctness regressions and KV-cache divergence when nodes opportunistically switched to lower-precision kernels under load. These issues were most pronounced during warm-up phases and when continuous-batching mixed short warm-up sequences with steady-state traffic. The goal of this PR is to make the low-precision fast path reliable in production by adding conservative checks and an automatic, observable annealing mechanism that trades small amounts of peak throughput for deterministic correctness.

Summary of changes: add a light-weight per-node kernel stability probe that runs microbenchmarks on model startup and periodically during low-utilization windows; expose a configurable 'kernel_stability_threshold' that gates transitions to low-precision kernels; implement a precision-annealing state machine that steps precision down gradually (fp32 -> fp16 -> int8) only when stability and latency criteria are met; add a kv-sync-guard which attaches short-lived checksums to KV cache snapshots and prevents applying a cache state if checksum mismatch or stale-timestamp detected; update continuous-batching heuristics to avoid batching sequences observed during the warm-up probe and to prefer homogeneous-decoded sequences to reduce cache churn.

Configuration and defaults: default kernel_stability_threshold=0.92 (fraction of microbench runs that must pass), anneal_step_interval=30s, min_stable_window=2m. Operators can override in runtime config or via console per-cluster. Canary rollout automatically enables annealing on 10% of nodes by default.

Design notes: stability probe is intentionally lightweight (per-model token-limited runs) and runs on a background worker with a low scheduling priority. We capture simple metrics: decode latency variance, kernel success/failure, and checksum of produced KV updates. The precision-annealing state machine records a rollback count and will automatically revert to the last-known-good precision if a regression is detected for two consecutive evaluation windows. KV-sync-guard uses a small 64-bit checksum and timestamp to detect divergent updates; it prevents a stale or corrupt cache from being applied and triggers a re-fetch path that is more conservative (sequential KV application with verification).

Performance and correctness: measured on internal perf-lab with a mix of 1k short-chat and 200 long-generation traces: baseline (optimistic fp16 fastpath without probes) showed +12.3% token/sec vs safe fp32 but a 2.8% rare correctness/regression signal on our eval set and occasional KV-invalidation incidents during canary. With this PR enabled (default canary), we observe +9.1% token/sec, p95 token latency improved by 6ms relative to safe fp32, and correctness regressions dropped to 0.12% (within noise). CPU/GPU telemetry indicates a ~7% reduction in wasted kernel restarts during warm-up.

Commits (summary):
- feat(kernel): add kernel stability probe, probe scheduler, and probe metrics (maya/commit/1)
- feat(anneal): implement precision-annealing state machine and runtime flags (maya/commit/2)
- fix(kv): implement kv-sync-guard with checksum verification and fallback path (alex/commit/3)
- perf(scheduler): adjust continuous-batching heuristic to avoid warm-up mixing (noah/commit/4)
- test(perf): new perf harness scenarios and canary harness (sofia/commit/5)
- docs: ops notes and runtime configuration docs (maya/commit/6)

Files touched (high level):
- src/runtime/kernel_probe.cpp (new)
- src/runtime/kernel_selector.cpp (modify)
- src/runtime/precision_annealer.cpp (new)
- src/cache/kv_manager.rs (modify)
- src/scheduler/batcher.rs (modify)
- tests/perf/annealing_scenarios.py (new)

Testing: unit tests added for state machine transitions and kv-sync checksum logic; integration canary runs in perf-lab for 48h; additional chaos test where random kernel failure is injected to validate rollback behavior. CI initially failed on a flaky kv-manager apply test (race in test harness); I fixed the test harness timing and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed (build, unit, integration-smoke, perf-canary sim).

Review conversation (high level):
- Andre Patel: "This looks promising — my main concern is metric noise causing oscillation. Can we add hysteresis?"
- Maya Chen: "Added rollback_count and min_stable_window config to prevent oscillation; updated tests to exercise noisy conditions."
- Sofia Lopez: "KV checksum is a good safety net. Can we make checksum optional for extremely latency-sensitive clusters?"
- Maya Chen: "Yes — checksum can be disabled per-cluster; documented tradeoffs in ops doc and console UI will show expected risk increase."
- Noah Kim: "Please ensure the annealer doesn't increase tail latency under multimodal traffic."
- Maya Chen: "Batcher heuristic update ensures warm-up sequences are isolated, avoiding mixed-batch tail effects; added perf tests that mimic multimodal traffic."
- Andre Patel: approved after minor doc nits.
- Sofia Lopez: approved.

CI and canary: initial canary run on 10% nodes for 72h showed stability; we increased to 30% and then full rollout. Post-rollout monitoring showed one transient kv-stall on a highly loaded node which was auto-rolled back by annealing and later resolved by a kernel patch (follow-up PR scheduled).

Backward compatibility and migration: all flags default to conservative values; clusters not opting into canary see no behavior change. Ops doc includes a migration checklist to enable annealing and KV checksum on dedicated clusters.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-2493: extend probe to multi-model ensembles (planned)
- SRE-619: dashboard and alerting on kernel stability score
- Hotfix PR planned to backport small kv-sync optimization to 2026.02 release branch if customers request earlier rollout.

Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-18 after approvals and green CI.

Notes for maintainers: keep an eye on SLO dashboards for the first 2 weeks after rollout; if automated rollback rates exceed 0.5% consider increasing min_stable_window or disabling annealing during peak traffic windows.
